chunks: It is God who created you from dust, then from a sperm, then formed you into pairs. Neither does a female conceive nor gives birth without His knowledge; nor do the old grow older or become younger in years but in accordance with the law (of nature). Indeed the law of God works inevitably.

key_terms.أَزْوَاجًا: Pairs, referring to male and female genders
key_terms.أُنثَىٰ: Female, specifically in the context of carrying a fetus
key_terms.تُرَابٍ: Dust, representing the initial material origin of creation
key_terms.عِلْمِهِ: His knowledge, indicating God's omniscience over biological processes
key_terms.كِتَابٍ: Book, referring to the divine record of decrees
key_terms.مُعَمَّرٍ: One who lives long, referring to the elderly
key_terms.نُّطْفَةٍ: A drop of fluid (semen), the second stage of embryonic development
key_terms.يَسِيرٌ: Easy or effortless, describing God's power

ai.seo_question: What are the stages of human creation and how does divine decree relate to lifespan in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Ar-Rum (often cited in discussions of creation) underscores the omnipotence of Allah in orchestrating human development from dust to paired genders, highlighting His precise knowledge over every biological nuance. The mention of the 'divine book' (Kitab) for lifespan and death reflects the concept of Al-Kutub al-Arba'ah, affirming that changes in life duration are pre-recorded by His will. This serves as a reminder of divine decree (Qadr) while maintaining human agency within the framework of God's easy command.
